criminal_detail: Patrick Heron was arrested three times between 2022 and 2023 and charged with more than 200 counts, including child sexual assault, sexual abuse of children, kidnapping of a minor, and official oppression. On October 20, 2023 he pleaded guilty to charges including unlawful contact with a minor, sexual abuse of children, involuntary deviate sexual intercourse, official oppression, kidnapping of a minor, indecent assault, forgery, and stalking, and was sentenced to 15 to 40 years in state prison.
incident_date_approx: circa 2005-2022, largely in Philadelphia's Kensington neighborhood
description: Patrick Heron served as a Philadelphia police officer for roughly 24 years before leaving the force in 2019. Prosecutors alleged that between about 2005 and 2022 he sexually assaulted 48 women and girls, most of whom remain unidentified, often targeting vulnerable people in the Kensington neighborhood while on duty and in uniform, and that he recorded dozens of assaults, including about 30 over a 13-month period in the back seat of his police vehicle. On October 20, 2023, Heron pleaded guilty to charges including unlawful contact with a minor, sexual abuse of children, involuntary deviate sexual intercourse, kidnapping of a minor, and official oppression, and was sentenced to 15 to 40 years in state prison. Despite the scale of the criminal case, dedicated searches found no public reporting of a filed civil lawsuit or formal claim against Heron, the Philadelphia Police Department, or the City of Philadelphia arising from this conduct as of July 2026.
inclusion_concern: No filed civil lawsuit or formal claim could be verified in public reporting. The seed's 2023 'ongoing' hint appears to reflect the criminal prosecution (resolved by guilty plea in October 2023), not civil litigation. Multiple dedicated searches for suits, notices of claim, or settlements involving Heron or the City of Philadelphia surfaced only criminal-case coverage.
